key_insight: A differentiable WMLES framework can jointly learn subgrid-scale and wall closures end-to-end, improving turbulence predictions because the closures and discretization are tightly coupled.
engineering_relevance: This enables reusable turbulence models that transfer across Reynolds numbers, grids, and domains, reducing the need to hand-tune separate wall and SGS closures for each simulation setup.
method: Train SGS and wall closures together inside a differentiable flow solver.
Use a neural network plus a fixed physics-preserving layer for each closure.
Optimize only from low-order statistics while backpropagating through the coupled CFD system.
evidence_signal: On a zero-pressure-gradient turbulent boundary layer, the model beats WMLES baselines across Re_θ = 600–6500, extrapolates beyond the training range, and transfers to unseen grids and domains while recovering both the log-law region and resolved spectra.
watch_item: The approach depends on differentiable solver infrastructure and careful joint training; learning either closure alone was insufficient, so implementation and optimization stability may be nontrivial.
paper_title: Differentiable Hybrid Neural-CFD Modelling of Wall-Bounded Turbulence: Coupled Learning of Subgrid-Scale and Wall Closures
